module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1008

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1008](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1008)
- [CFS14b] Conlon, D. and Fox, J. and Sudakov, B., *Large subgraphs without complete bipartite
  graphs*. arXiv:1401.6711 (2014).
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
-/

@[expose] public section

open SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos1008

/--
Does every graph with $m$ edges contain a subgraph with $\gg m^{2/3}$ edges which contains
no $C_4$?

This problem was first solved in the affirmative by Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov [CFS14b]. A simple
proof is given by Hunter in the comments.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1008.lean"]
theorem erdos_1008 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ H ≤ G, (cycleGraph 4).Free H ∧
        c * (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) ≤ (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Originally asked by Bollobás and Erdős in 'a colloquium on graph theory at Tihany' with $m^{2/3}$
replaced by $m^{3/4}$. Folkman showed this is false with the counterexample $K_{n,n^2}$, which has
$n^3$ edges, and yet every subgraph with $>n^2+\binom{n}{2}$ edges contains a $C_4$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1008.variants.three_quarters : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ H ≤ G, (cycleGraph 4).Free H ∧
        c * (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Folkman's counterexample $K_{n,n^2}$, which has $n^3$ edges, and yet every subgraph with
$>n^2+\binom{n}{2}$ edges contains a $C_4$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1008.variants.folkman (n : ℕ) :
    ((completeBipartiteGraph (Fin n) (Fin (n ^ 2))).edgeSet.ncard = n ^ 3) ∧
      ∀ H ≤ completeBipartiteGraph (Fin n) (Fin (n ^ 2)),
        n ^ 2 + n.choose 2 < H.edgeSet.ncard → cycleGraph 4 ⊑ H := by
  sorry

/--
In [Er71] Erdős revises the conjecture to $m^{2/3}$, and notes $\gg m^{1/2}$ is trivial.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1008.variants.lower_bound :
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ H ≤ G, (cycleGraph 4).Free H ∧
        c * (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1008

findings.description: The docstring at line 41 says that Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov first solved the problem. The cited 1971 paper already credits Szemerédi with the same m^(2/3) bound in its note added in proof. This is a historical attribution error, not a defect in the Lean statement or its solved status.
findings.source_evidence: [Er71], Problem 1, p. 97, footnote: “Note added in proof: Szemerédi proved cn^{2/3}.” https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1971-25.pdf
findings.suggested_fix: Remove “first”, or credit Szemerédi using the note added in proof to [Er71] and describe [CFS14b] as a later proof. No change to the theorem, answer, or category is needed.

reformulations.difference: The witness H ≤ G is a spanning subgraph on G's vertex type, whereas the source permits an arbitrary subgraph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An arbitrary C4-free subgraph can be extended to all vertices of G by adding isolated vertices. This preserves its edge count and cannot introduce C4, whose vertices all have neighbors. Conversely, a spanning subgraph is an ordinary subgraph. The pointwise equivalence for any real edge-count threshold was proved as spanning_vs_ordinary in the scratch file; therefore the same uniform positive constant works in both formulations.

reformulations.difference: The proposed m^(3/4) guarantee uses spanning subgraphs rather than arbitrary subgraphs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The scratch lemma spanning_vs_ordinary proves equivalence of the subgraph-existence predicates without changing the edge threshold. Thus the uniformly quantified guarantees, and consequently their negations expressed by answer(False), are equivalent.

reformulations.difference: The universal containment assertion ranges over spanning subgraphs of K_{n,n²}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Adding isolated vertices to an arbitrary subgraph preserves both its edge count and whether it contains C4. The scratch lemma universal_spanning_vs_ordinary proves the universal threshold-containment equivalence. Specializing it to K_{n,n²} and n² + choose(n,2) gives the source's assertion.

reformulations.difference: The m^(1/2) lower bound asks for a spanning C4-free subgraph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same edge-preserving isolated-vertex extension proves equivalence with an arbitrary C4-free subgraph. The threshold-parametric scratch lemma spanning_vs_ordinary covers this exponent as well.

sources_consulted: Conlon–Fox–Sudakov, Large subgraphs without complete bipartite graphs, arXiv:1401.6711, especially Theorem 2.1, Theorem 2.3, and the remark identifying K_{2,2} with C4; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1401.6711
Erdős, Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis (1971), Problem 1 and its note added in proof, p. 97: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1971-25.pdf
Rényi Institute Erdős bibliography, entry 1971-25: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html
Linked formal proof, including is_C4 and exists_C4_free_subgraph_with_many_edges: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plby/lean-proofs/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1008.lean

review.notes: All four mathematical statements are faithful. Checked quantifier scope, answer polarity, ordinary versus induced containment, real exponents, and finite edge cardinalities. Scratch checks compile successfully: C4 has four edges; K_{n,n²} has n³ edges for every n; the n=0 and n=1 Folkman thresholds are unreachable; empty graphs satisfy the stated lower-bound boundary cases. Exhaustive bipartite edge-subset tests give maximum C4-free sizes 0, 1, and 5 for n=0,1,2. The linked external formal proof also compiled successfully, and its final theorem uses only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The live erdosproblems.com problem and forum pages returned Cloudflare challenges, so their current wording and the Hunter-comment attribution could not be independently checked; the cited primary papers suffice to verify all four mathematical statements and their solved status.
